fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can quickly distinguish it from the main residence during an incident.
• Keep the area immediately in front of and around the parking areas clear of parked vehicles when possible to allow responder equipment and personnel to move between structures.
• Trim any shrubs or plantings in the landscaped areas that overhang or narrow the walkway connecting the main residence and detached structure.
• Post the property address at the single access point so it is readable from both directions of approach.
• Keep the perimeter fencing gates unlocked or secured with a breakaway latch to allow responders to reach the rear and sides of both structures without delay.
• Clear a turning area near the end of the driveway or parking area so emergency vehicles can reverse out without obstructing the single access point.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to either structure so responders can move around the building perimeters without obstruction.
• Keep the open lawn area free of stored materials or equipment that would block responder staging near the structures.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters near the structures to create more open space between the trees and the buildings.
• Remove or trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching any structure.
• Clear out the vegetation growing between structures to reduce the chance of fire moving from one building to another.
• Thin scattered trees across the property to reduce the amount of connected plant material that could carry fire toward the structures.
• Trim low-hanging branches on trees near the structures so flames cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Keep scattered shrubs mowed or cut back, particularly those within close range of any building.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so vehicles can move freely.
• Maintain the open terrain areas by preventing new shrub or tree growth from filling in those gaps over time.
